name: Depth-Anything-V2-Small-hf
creator: depth-anything
old_description_hint: Depth Anything V2 Small for monocular depth estimation. Trained on 595K synthetic + 62M unlabeled real images. Best at: zero-shot depth prediction with fine-grained details and robustness. Domains: 3D reconstruction, robotics, autonomous systems. Typical uses: depth map generation, 3D scene understanding. Not suited for: metric depth without calibration.

name: DA3METRIC-LARGE
creator: depth-anything
old_description_hint: Depth Anything 3 Metric Large for metric depth estimation in monocular settings. 350M parameter model. Best at: real-world scale depth prediction with camera intrinsics and poses. Capabilities: relative depth, metric depth, sky segmentation. Typical uses: 3D mapping, real estate analysis. Not suited for: video sequences without temporal consistency.

name: layoutlm-document-qa
creator: impira
old_description_hint: LayoutLM fine-tuned on SQuAD 2.0 and DocVQA for document visual question answering. Best at: Extracting answers from document images using text and layout understanding. Domains: Business documents, invoices, forms, receipts. Typical uses: Invoice field extraction, receipt parsing, document-based information retrieval. Not suited for: Pure text QA, images without structured layout.

name: layoutlm-invoices
creator: impira
old_description_hint: LayoutLM fine-tuned on invoices with non-consecutive token extraction capability. Best at: Question answering on invoices, extracting multi-line fields and addresses. Domains: Financial documents, invoice processing, business document automation. Typical uses: Automated invoice processing, line-item extraction, multi-field address capture. Not suited for: General document QA, non-structured text extraction.

name: donut-base-finetuned-docvqa
creator: naver-clova-ix
old_description_hint: Donut model (Swin Transformer encoder + BART decoder) fine-tuned on DocVQA for OCR-free document understanding. Best at: Document visual question answering without requiring explicit OCR. Domains: Document intelligence, form understanding, business document processing. Typical uses: Form field extraction, document classification, visual layout understanding. Not suited for: Text-only QA, non-document images, real-time processing.

name: MoLFormer-XL-both-10pct
creator: ibm-research
old_description_hint: IBM's transformer model trained on SMILES representations of molecules from ZINC and PubChem for molecular property prediction. Best at: extracting meaningful embeddings and representations of small molecules. Domains: chemistry, drug discovery, materials science. Typical uses: molecular property prediction, similarity search, fine-tuning for toxicity and solubility prediction. Not suited for: molecule generation; molecules larger than ~200 atoms.

name: codebert-base
creator: microsoft
old_description_hint: Microsoft's bidirectional code-to-documentation embedding model trained on CodeSearchNet. Best at: semantic code search and matching code to documentation. Domains: software development. Typical uses: finding relevant code snippets by natural language query, code-to-doc retrieval, program synthesis assistance. Not suited for: code generation or completion.

name: nucleotide-transformer-v2-500m-multi-species
creator: InstaDeepAI
old_description_hint: InstaDeepAI's 500M-parameter transformer pretrained on DNA sequences from 850 diverse genomes for genomic representation learning. Best at: extracting meaningful embeddings from DNA sequences across species. Domains: genomics, genetic research, evolutionary biology. Typical uses: predicting molecular phenotypes, disease association prediction, comparative genomics analysis. Not suited for: plants, viruses, or sequences exceeding design specifications.

name: Bio_ClinicalBERT
creator: emilyalsentzer
old_description_hint: BioBERT-based language model pre-trained on MIMIC III clinical notes from ICU patients. Best at: downstream clinical NLP tasks including entity recognition, question answering, and text classification on clinical documents. Domains: clinical healthcare, biomedical research. Typical uses: clinical text understanding, medical record analysis, healthcare NLP applications. Not suited for: non-clinical text or general-domain language modeling.

name: esm2_t33_650M_UR50D
creator: facebook
old_description_hint: Meta's ESM-2 protein language model with 650M parameters trained via masked language modeling on protein sequences. Best at: learning protein representations and sequence embeddings. Domains: structural biology, protein research. Typical uses: fine-tuning for protein property prediction, secondary structure prediction, protein function classification. Not suited for: protein structure prediction (use ESMFold instead).

name: BiomedNLP-BiomedBERT-base-uncased-abstract-fulltext
creator: microsoft
old_description_hint: BERT pre-trained on PubMed abstracts and full-text articles for comprehensive biomedical understanding. Best at: Biomedical NLP tasks spanning both abstracts and complete papers. Domains: Biomedical research, medical publishing, literature mining, life sciences. Typical uses: Full-text literature mining, biomedical information extraction, paper classification. Not suited for: General English NLP, non-medical domains, real-time applications.

name: codebert-base-mlm
creator: microsoft
old_description_hint: Microsoft's code embedding model trained with masked language modeling objective for code completion tasks. Best at: predicting missing tokens in code sequences. Domains: software development. Typical uses: code completion, code token prediction, fine-tuning on downstream programming tasks. Not suited for: semantic code search without adaptation.
